title: Quarter roadmap: hypothesis backlog & risk catalog for Private/VPC rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures the quarter-level hypothesis backlog, gating criteria, and prioritized risk catalog for the Private/VPC/on-prem feature set. It is intended to be the single source of truth for which hypotheses we will validate in the quarter to derisk rollout waves and to translate OKRs into measurable experiments and engineering work.
background: Enterprise customers require deterministic upgrade windows, network isolation, and observability comparable to hosted offerings. Historically we've shipped features with technical debt that increases upgrade friction for Private instances. This quarter we shift from feature delivery to hypothesis validation: each roadmap item must have a defined success metric, a safety gate, and a rollback plan.
objectives: Define top 6 product hypotheses that materially reduce upgrade risk or onboarding time for Private customers
Create a ranked experiment backlog that maps to existing engineering capacity and Dedicated release lanes
Establish clear gating criteria for canary->wave promotion and a risk register with mitigations
Enable quantifiable OKR signals to track progress against reliability and time-to-onboard goals
success_metrics: Reduce mean time to onboard Private customers from 18 days to <= 10 days
Decrease upgrade rollback rate for private waves from 6% to <= 2%
Achieve 95th percentile API latency parity with hosted baseline for 90% of customer workloads
All top-6 hypotheses have an experiment or pilot started by end of cycle
milestones: Week 1: Hypothesis workshops with sales/solutions to capture customer failure modes
Week 2: Prioritization session using RICE + regulatory weightings
Week 3-5: Engineering spikes and pilot builds for top 3 hypotheses
Week 6: Canary planning + runbook updates and security gating
Week 8-10: Pilot cohort launches and metric collection
Week 12: Retro, decision to promote to wave or continue iteration
acceptance_criteria: Each roadmap item includes: user problem statement, hypothesis, target metric, UX/ops change required, rollback path
Runbooks updated and validated with on-call for any automated rollouts
Security checklist completed (KMS, audit logs, network controls) and signed off by Security
Pilot demonstrates target metric movement with signal quality sufficient to make promote/hold decision
risks: Underspecified integration contracts between control plane and customer VPC causing intermittent failures
Resource contention on dedicated pools during pilot leading to noisy signals
Compliance dependencies (customer KMS integrations) slowing pilot sign-ups
Inadequate telemetry for per-route error attribution in private instances
mitigation_actions: Add a lightweight compatibility check tool to run prior to pilot enrollment
Reserve burst capacity for pilot cohorts and instrument queuing metrics
Create a prioritized list of customers with pre-validated KMS setups for early pilots
Ship a focused telemetry shim to capture trace-id propagation across control plane <> dataplane
stakeholders: Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Luca Moreno (PM lead)
Engineering: Rajiv Singh (runtime), Mei Chen (ops), Priya Rao (security integrations)

updates: 2026-02-22: Workshop completed with Solutions + Sales; captured 14 customer failure modes and mapped to 9 candidate hypotheses.
2026-02-26: Prioritization run using RICE; top 6 hypotheses selected and owners assigned.
2026-03-03: Engineering spike 1 (control plane compatibility check) finished; preliminary tool prototype in GH PR #8721.
2026-03-10: Security reviewed KMS integration patterns; requested proof-of-concept using HSM-backed test key for two customers. Action assigned to Priya Rao.
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Prefer pilot-first releases with reserved capacity vs broad dark-launch to minimize noisy signals.
Tradeoff: Slower initial adoption for pilots, but higher confidence on upgrade safety and fewer rollbacks.
Follow-up: Create a lightweight customer consent template for telemetry collection during pilots. Owner: Hannah Brooks.
